content.title: About
content.content: Date is the sweet fruit of the date palm (Phoenix dactylifera), native to the arid regions of the Middle East, North Africa, and South Asia. The fruits are dark brown, soft‑fleshed, and have a characteristic caramel‑like sweetness.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The date palm can reach up to 30 m in height and live for more than 150 years.
Dates have been cultivated for over 6 000 years, making them one of the oldest cultivated crops.
There are more than 200 varieties of dates, differing in size, color, and sweetness level.
Dates are often called a “natural energy bar” because of their high natural sugar content.
In ancient cultures dates were used in rituals and offered as gifts to deities.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Dates provide both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting healthy digestion and blood‑sugar regulation.

items.title: High in potassium
items.content: Potassium helps maintain fluid balance, blood pressure, and proper muscle function.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids, carotenoids, and phenolic compounds protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Heart‑friendly nutrients
items.content: Monounsaturated fats and magnesium contribute to lower LDL cholesterol levels.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: Vitamins B6, B5, and folate are involved in energy metabolism and red blood‑cell formation.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Because dates are rich in natural sugars, they can raise the glycemic index and should be limited by people with diabetes.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Dates are calorie‑dense; excessive consumption may lead to weight gain.

items.title: Allergy potential
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to dates.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: High oxalate levels may contribute to kidney‑stone formation in susceptible individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Dates can be eaten as a snack, added to cereals, yogurt, smoothies, baked goods, or used as a natural sweetener. They are often stuffed with nuts, cheese, or chocolate.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dates in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For long‑term storage, keep them in the refrigerator or freezer, where they stay fresh for up to a year.
